contributions.statement: When agents infer pre/postconditions for legacy code, accept a contract only after it survives property/fuzz runs lifted from the existing unit tests (for Java, e.g. Jazzer or jqwik), not the unit tests alone: fuzzing rejected 8.0% of unit-test-passing contracts in the weaker-tested repo (0.4% in the well-tested one).
contributions.evidence: §4 'Impact of Fuzzing', Table 3: BDE vs BlazingMQ survivors of the unit-test filter that fuzzing then violated. Two C++ repos from the authors' organization, single greedy runs.
relative_to: property-based / fuzz testing beyond example-based tests

contributions.statement: Reject agent-synthesized contracts or assertions that reduce to 'true' as a separate gate check, since up to 17% of 'valid' contracts were trivially true.
contributions.evidence: Table 1 'Trivial' column (BMQ, Qwen3.5: 17.13%), noted by the audit as inflating the 85% validity headline.
relative_to: 2606.18168 assertion-free agent tests are not verification

contributions.statement: Cap counterexample-guided refinement at roughly 20 attempts per function; most gains arrive in the first five.
contributions.evidence: Fig. 6: valid-spec count vs retry attempts on BDE for one model configuration.
relative_to: P16 execution-based verifier loops (2609.03086 diminishing returns after first attempts)

reason: The C++/separation-logic machinery does not transfer, but 'lift unit tests into fuzz oracles and reject trivial contracts' is a concrete gate for back-filling contracts before spec-driven work. The 10x cost headline is a pricing artifact and is not used.
